correctness.rationale: Complete proof: for even n=2t (t>=2) the integer relation lattice has basis r=(t+1,-t,0), s=(0,2t+3,-(2t+1)), length increments 1 and 2. For odd n=2t+1 (t>=1) it has basis r=(2t+3,-(2t+1),0), s=(0,t+2,-(t+1)), increments 2 and 1. Modular gcd computations prove these are full lattices. For any ordered same-fiber factorization pair, three exhaustive sign cases express displacement as nonnegative sums of value-preserving moves with nonnegative length increments; in mixed-sign cases moves are coordinate-conformal, and in the all-positive case applying s before r preserves feasibility. Maximum move distance is 2n+3. For the lower bound the primitive equal-length relation (n+2,-(2n+3),n+1) has two disjoint nonnegative endpoints of length 2n+3 and exactly two equal-length factorizations in its fiber; monotone chains between equal-length endpoints cannot leave that length. An executable independent enumeration cross-checked n=3..15 and 2923 factorization pairs and primitive fibers. No step extrapolates finite tests.

value.rationale: A natural complete exact factorization invariant for an infinite sequence-defined numerical semigroup family: the monotone catenary degree controls length-nondecreasing conversion between representations, a more stringent question than the previously studied ordinary catenary degree. An explicit primitive equal-length witness and a uniform directed algorithm establish sharpness and structural mechanism. The formula grows linearly with n and is not just a low-index enumeration or restatement of the published two undirected relations. Motivated by the 2017 complete presentation and the 2026 emphasis on catenary invariants for consecutive triangular generators. It does not claim a general statement for four-generator or other polynomial families.
